subject: English
title: CISCE curriculum: English, Class VII

source.read: A third-party web page that sets out the Class VII English syllabus of the CISCE curriculum, published by BYJU'S (page numbers are not given)
source.note: UNOFFICIAL SOURCE. The page gives the year as 2023-24 and names no publisher for the syllabus itself; it was read through a text summary of the page. The official document on cisce.org could not be reached from the build environment. CISCE is understood not to prescribe a textbook for this class, so a school's own book and term plan may order or extend these topics.

licence: Strand names as printed (facts). Every outcome is written by OpenPath in its own words with a pointer to its strand and line; no curriculum text is reproduced.
review: OpenPath curriculum inventory (research from a secondary source; not an educator review)

outcomes.text: Listens to stories, poems, speeches and dialogues and understands them.
Follows the issues in lectures, debates and group discussions.
outcomes.note: Done aloud with a grown-up, who ticks what they heard. The app cannot hear or mark speaking.

outcomes.text: Reads literary and other texts on a wide range of themes, from home and community to science, media and the environment.
outcomes.note: Long reads: six stories in three parts each, on home, community, science, the environment, media and history, with questions on each part and on the whole. The Reading course adds its own stories and reports.

outcomes.text: Reads widely and closely, for understanding and for what is implied.
Analyses vocabulary, figurative language, tone and mood.
outcomes.note: Practised on short extracts of two or three sentences, not on whole texts.

outcomes.text: Looks at how authors build their texts.
outcomes.note: Practised on short extracts of two or three sentences, not on whole texts.

outcomes.text: Reads from a suggested list of novels, short stories, life stories and graphic novels.
outcomes.note: The suggested books are published works and are not in the app. The learner reads one and tells a grown-up about it; the app's own stories are in Reading.

outcomes.text: Writes messages, invitations, short paragraphs, formal and informal letters, and applications.
outcomes.note: Written here or on paper to a task set for this class. The learner checks it against a short list and a grown-up ticks what they see. The app does not keep or mark the writing; the essay studio gives a closer analysis where an evaluator is connected.
